The body primarily metabolizes isopropyl alcohol (isopropanol) in the liver via the enzyme **alcohol dehydrogenase** into **acetone** , while excreting a substantial portion unchanged. Unlike methanol or ethylene glycol, acetone is a neutral ketone rather than an acid, so metabolism generally causes ketosis without high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXX1e4hLzf1jKUjBR51zecVqAPnlx1wO5sXqN8lVHQXVLNQEJpRq1Mn4XuhxlBYf7hHkgqUYjGbpo5KntF6S7fyJQlwfAw4cE9b7X83e6KNxYPaYTtIkZZJYXVxnASJ60Qlu1-evw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESWgHEIkXXuk26TF6Ya7tp543XMFRR1_vnjQ03NPgGduvp2MkaSaKkL3s4WFMYlVt_KFYdzWMkVr7T-qD4zUjA-fqK5-xGUSrMX9AJ0MUAgtV99IVdGKzzgq3Cag)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHEIkXXu3lQg9O1_ycCgaHd5PqnfcTRu05u9xaWLbmcKUDWZ0Zacess2IxWsxw4Sjggh_b_s8LV4rnwkZgtlaIqW2VUbvN0VocTfG-WeasokAYVsF9hssGmM_iXBP6vjuWWfzkutM8bwqa0Gm-QpI9-kBow7Q)

### Absorption and Distribution

- **Rapid uptake:** Isopropyl alcohol is absorbed quickly across the gastrointestinal tract (peaking in blood around 30–120 minutes after ingestion) and can also enter through the skin or inhalation.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXMZLWGz-F6wvpGi7rZqtaEtWVV6Y_U1l-HFiN32w-1NUR7tvlElsgdhEhpG7Z15GRlNOQ4E9t-b2THl_guXPDU5Vil2X-izrBNPKmYhWl_N4yXFWG22s8BZocdhktl4F2)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESWgHEIkXXuk26TF6Ya7tp543XMFRR1_vnjQ03NPgGduvp2MkaSaKkL3s4WFMYlVt_KFYdzWMkVr7T-qD4zUjA-fqK5-xGUSrMX9AJ0MUAgtV99IVdGKzzgq3Cag)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXXCDOSgzKq14XwFZuC4xNebPUM3cdgDQAI_LkRr8lZ2YXafYaOKkGZABKzMSd_0ikQlKEHqoYgvmdkZiPPInkGQ6duRm7JX1xsgMsy-JO1_UfPpVGbrxc85rwSdl60yy8w2Z_po2hhrfPHDWNrFg)
- **Body water distribution:** It distributes widely in body water with an apparent volume of distribution of about **0.6 to 0.7 L/kg** , taking roughly two hours for full tissue distribution.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHEIkXXu3lQg9O1_ycCgaHd5PqnfcTRu05u9xaWLbmcKUDWZ0Zacess2IxWsxw4Sjggh_b_s8LV4rnwkZgtlaIqW2VUbvN0VocTfG-WeasokAYVsF9hssGmM_iXBP6vjuWWfzkutM8bwqa0Gm-QpI9-kBow7Q)
- **Potency:** Because it is slightly larger and less polar than ethanol, it crosses into the central nervous system readily and acts as a stronger CNS depressant.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXX1e4hLzf1jKUjBR51zecVqAPnlx1wO5sXqN8lVHQXVLNQEJpRq1Mn4XuhxlBYf7hHkgqUYjGbpo5KntF6S7fyJQlwfAw4cE9b7X83e6KNxYPaYTtIkZZJYXVxnASJ60Qlu1-evw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF19A6lB7d-nE73oSvw5twyzRpO50chhFmVxFFP5fGC4grDVQaJwZgjjvECVA5yvpLDinaguAzxxWCvCl0d0Af9H0F-Q82VV469aeEPIRzye-PDBqZ108I8aqLzq2rhWe4uKdl6sBZyD_qz02oH87SzHAVD42JbzdGpHs2SQ)

### Metabolic Pathway and Kinetics

- **Conversion to acetone:** Most absorbed isopropanol is oxidized by hepatic alcohol dehydrogenase to **acetone** , which reaches peak blood levels several hours after exposure (often around 4 hours). Acetone itself depresses the CNS and prolongs sedation and intoxication.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXX1e4hLzf1jKUjBR51zecVqAPnlx1wO5sXqN8lVHQXVLNQEJpRq1Mn4XuhxlBYf7hHkgqUYjGbpo5KntF6S7fyJQlwfAw4cE9b7X83e6KNxYPaYTtIkZZJYXVxnASJ60Qlu1-evw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXXCDOSgzKq14XwFZuC4xNebPUM3cdgDQAI_LkRr8lZ2YXafYaOKkGZABKzMSd_0ikQlKEHqoYgvmdkZiPPInkGQ6duRm7JX1xsgMsy-JO1_UfPpVGbrxc85rwSdl60yy8w2Z_po2hhrfPHDWNrFg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHEIkXXu3lQg9O1_ycCgaHd5PqnfcTRu05u9xaWLbmcKUDWZ0Zacess2IxWsxw4Sjggh_b_s8LV4rnwkZgtlaIqW2VUbvN0VocTfG-WeasokAYVsF9hssGmM_iXBP6vjuWWfzkutM8bwqa0Gm-QpI9-kBow7Q)
- **Half-life and kinetics:** Isopropyl alcohol typically follows first-order elimination with a blood half-life of roughly **2.5 to 3.2 hours** (slower than typical ethanol clearance). Acetone clears much more slowly, with a reported human elimination half-life around **22 hours**.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZAHEIkXXGEMstk31rKyqPPCkmQaPGBNMy5gKkyOK8tvkIkae-JWStlSjRs3VQaeBtM9ccGoFJNFifQ2WD9k1htz7sASQ9coDyu2clq5JFuLW5eV6S5tdaZgfJBZdq9d7Oq8fqZA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHEIkXXu3lQg9O1_ycCgaHd5PqnfcTRu05u9xaWLbmcKUDWZ0Zacess2IxWsxw4Sjggh_b_s8LV4rnwkZgtlaIqW2VUbvN0VocTfG-WeasokAYVsF9hssGmM_iXBP6vjuWWfzkutM8bwqa0Gm-QpI9-kBow7Q)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF19A6lB7d-nE73oSvw5twyzRpO50chhFmVxFFP5fGC4grDVQaJwZgjjvECVA5yvpLDinaguAzxxWCvCl0d0Af9H0F-Q82VV469aeEPIRzye-PDBqZ108I8aqLzq2rhWe4uKdl6sBZyD_qz02oH87SzHAVD42JbzdGpHs2SQ)
- **Elimination:** Roughly **20% to 50%** of an absorbed dose is excreted unchanged (primarily via the kidneys and a small fraction in exhaled air). Acetone leaves the body slowly through the lungs and kidneys.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESWgHEIkXXuk26TF6Ya7tp543XMFRR1_vnjQ03NPgGduvp2MkaSaKkL3s4WFMYlVt_KFYdzWMkVr7T-qD4zUjA-fqK5-xGUSrMX9AJ0MUAgtV99IVdGKzzgq3Cag)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHEIkXXu3lQg9O1_ycCgaHd5PqnfcTRu05u9xaWLbmcKUDWZ0Zacess2IxWsxw4Sjggh_b_s8LV4rnwkZgtlaIqW2VUbvN0VocTfG-WeasokAYVsF9hssGmM_iXBP6vjuWWfzkutM8bwqa0Gm-QpI9-kBow7Q)

### Key Lab and Clinical Differences

- **Osmolal gap:** Both isopropyl alcohol and acetone raise serum osmolality, creating an elevated osmolal gap.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXX1e4hLzf1jKUjBR51zecVqAPnlx1wO5sXqN8lVHQXVLNQEJpRq1Mn4XuhxlBYf7hHkgqUYjGbpo5KntF6S7fyJQlwfAw4cE9b7X83e6KNxYPaYTtIkZZJYXVxnASJ60Qlu1-evw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHEIkXXu3lQg9O1_ycCgaHd5PqnfcTRu05u9xaWLbmcKUDWZ0Zacess2IxWsxw4Sjggh_b_s8LV4rnwkZgtlaIqW2VUbvN0VocTfG-WeasokAYVsF9hssGmM_iXBP6vjuWWfzkutM8bwqa0Gm-QpI9-kBow7Q)
- **Acid-base balance:** Because acetone is uncharged and does not form toxic organic acids, isopropanol poisoning typically causes ketonemia/ketonuria **without** severe metabolic acidosis (unless another condition, such as alcoholic ketoacidosis, is also present).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXeVrQ9F-YFvwbssNSJ5eVgUoiNyNayahszmX6Vo8hiPI2iqIa_SlUJiAhaGJ42WcUkd_cnClEg_ZOlNWI9s3MOpFztdRjyF_EJ0FmZ0crU2-v1O2eEBahzIjerHHlVhJrYCK2CE_PTQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXX1e4hLzf1jKUjBR51zecVqAPnlx1wO5sXqN8lVHQXVLNQEJpRq1Mn4XuhxlBYf7hHkgqUYjGbpo5KntF6S7fyJQlwfAw4cE9b7X83e6KNxYPaYTtIkZZJYXVxnASJ60Qlu1-evw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHEIkXXu3lQg9O1_ycCgaHd5PqnfcTRu05u9xaWLbmcKUDWZ0Zacess2IxWsxw4Sjggh_b_s8LV4rnwkZgtlaIqW2VUbvN0VocTfG-WeasokAYVsF9hssGmM_iXBP6vjuWWfzkutM8bwqa0Gm-QpI9-kBow7Q)
- **Treatment contrast:** Blocking alcohol dehydrogenase (such as with fomepizole) is used for methanol or ethylene glycol, but it slows isopropanol clearance and prolongs intoxication.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXeVrQ9F-YFvwbssNSJ5eVgUoiNyNayahszmX6Vo8hiPI2iqIa_SlUJiAhaGJ42WcUkd_cnClEg_ZOlNWI9s3MOpFztdRjyF_EJ0FmZ0crU2-v1O2eEBahzIjerHHlVhJrYCK2CE_PTQ)

For detailed medical toxicology context, see the [StatPearls Isopropanol Toxicity guide](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXX1e4hLzf1jKUjBR51zecVqAPnlx1wO5sXqN8lVHQXVLNQEJpRq1Mn4XuhxlBYf7hHkgqUYjGbpo5KntF6S7fyJQlwfAw4cE9b7X83e6KNxYPaYTtIkZZJYXVxnASJ60Qlu1-evw) or the [LITFL Isopropanol summary](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESWgHEIkXXuk26TF6Ya7tp543XMFRR1_vnjQ03NPgGduvp2MkaSaKkL3s4WFMYlVt_KFYdzWMkVr7T-qD4zUjA-fqK5-xGUSrMX9AJ0MUAgtV99IVdGKzzgq3Cag). *(If you or someone else has been exposed to isopropyl alcohol and has concerning symptoms, contact Poison Control or seek emergency medical care right away.)* [[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeQHEIkXXQ1Eocf9PDH6sqe7FTP-IR9Hnq0VrEH9wHl_VjVoaCE4iAoKxTYXQk28IwWirVufHA5lnl0tZ4SxqfkWDfwovrr-tDWXNFGJXS2W4mJzuSOL38ZBTX_KK_jqk4dWVn7lbpgE_bjoucUa_LkXTFbiZXVh0Jic)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXX1e4hLzf1jKUjBR51zecVqAPnlx1wO5sXqN8lVHQXVLNQEJpRq1Mn4XuhxlBYf7hHkgqUYjGbpo5KntF6S7fyJQlwfAw4cE9b7X83e6KNxYPaYTtIkZZJYXVxnASJ60Qlu1-evw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESWgHEIkXXuk26TF6Ya7tp543XMFRR1_vnjQ03NPgGduvp2MkaSaKkL3s4WFMYlVt_KFYdzWMkVr7T-qD4zUjA-fqK5-xGUSrMX9AJ0MUAgtV99IVdGKzzgq3Cag)[[4]](https://missouripoisoncenter.org/video/why-is-rubbing-alcohol-poisonous/)Are you looking into **specific biochemical steps**, **how it compares to ethanol or other toxic alcohols** , or **clinical signs and lab findings** of exposure?

- **Osmolal gap:** Both isopropyl alcohol and acetone raise serum osmolality, creating an elevated osmolal gap.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXX1e4hLzf1jKUjBR51zecVqAPnlx1wO5sXqN8lVHQXVLNQEJpRq1Mn4XuhxlBYf7hHkgqUYjGbpo5KntF6S7fyJQlwfAw4cE9b7X83e6KNxYPaYTtIkZZJYXVxnASJ60Qlu1-evw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHEIkXXu3lQg9O1_ycCgaHd5PqnfcTRu05u9xaWLbmcKUDWZ0Zacess2IxWsxw4Sjggh_b_s8LV4rnwkZgtlaIqW2VUbvN0VocTfG-WeasokAYVsF9hssGmM_iXBP6vjuWWfzkutM8bwqa0Gm-QpI9-kBow7Q)
- **Acid-base balance:** Because acetone is uncharged and does not form toxic organic acids, isopropanol poisoning typically causes ketonemia/ketonuria **without** severe metabolic acidosis (unless another condition, such as alcoholic ketoacidosis, is also present).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXeVrQ9F-YFvwbssNSJ5eVgUoiNyNayahszmX6Vo8hiPI2iqIa_SlUJiAhaGJ42WcUkd_cnClEg_ZOlNWI9s3MOpFztdRjyF_EJ0FmZ0crU2-v1O2eEBahzIjerHHlVhJrYCK2CE_PTQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHEIkXX1e4hLzf1jKUjBR51zecVqAPnlx1wO5sXqN8lVHQXVLNQEJpRq1Mn4XuhxlBYf7hHkgqUYjGbpo5KntF6S7fyJQlwfAw4cE9b7X83e6KNxYPaYTtIkZZJYXVxnASJ60Qlu1-evw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHEIkXXu3lQg9O1_ycCgaHd5PqnfcTRu05u9xaWLbmcKUDWZ0Zacess2IxWsxw4Sjggh_b_s8LV4rnwkZgtlaIqW2VUbvN0VocTfG-WeasokAYVsF9hssGmM_iXBP6vjuWWfzkutM8bwqa0Gm-QpI9-kBow7Q)
- **Treatment contrast:** Blocking alcohol dehydrogenase (such as with fomepizole) is used for methanol or ethylene glycol, but it slows isopropanol clearance and prolongs intoxication.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXeVrQ9F-YFvwbssNSJ5eVgUoiNyNayahszmX6Vo8hiPI2iqIa_SlUJiAhaGJ42WcUkd_cnClEg_ZOlNWI9s3MOpFztdRjyF_EJ0FmZ0crU2-v1O2eEBahzIjerHHlVhJrYCK2CE_PTQ)
